questions.q: What record is an Experience Cloud user's identity typically tied to, beyond the User record itself?
options: A Permission Set Group only
A Chatter Group
A Campaign record
A Contact record, and through it, an Account
questions.explain: Experience Cloud users are almost always tied to an underlying Contact, and through the Contact, to an Account — typically the customer's or partner's company — which is what drives their data visibility.

questions.q: Why does the Contact/Account linkage matter so much for Experience Cloud identity?
options: It is the authorization boundary — it determines which records (cases, orders, opportunities) tied to that Account the user is allowed to see
It only affects the user's display name
It is used solely for billing purposes
It doesn't matter; Experience Cloud users have no relationship to Accounts
questions.explain: The Contact/Account linkage directly drives sharing — an external user's visibility is scoped to records associated with their Contact's Account, making this link both an identity fact and an authorization boundary at once.

questions.q: Can different Experience Cloud sites in the same org have different login/self-registration behavior from each other and from the internal org?
options: Self-registration is never allowed on Experience Cloud sites
No, every site and the internal org must share identical login configuration
Yes — each site can have its own branding, login options, and self-registration behavior, independent of other sites and the internal org
Only one Experience Cloud site is allowed per org
questions.explain: A single org can run a customer site with open self-registration and social sign-on alongside a partner site requiring admin-approved invitation only — each site's identity configuration is independent.

questions.q: What is a 'community admin' role, in the delegated-administration pattern?
options: A bot account used for automated testing
A role that only applies to Chatter moderation
An internal Salesforce System Administrator with full org access
A delegated role letting a partner manage users within their own Account hierarchy, without granting internal Salesforce admin rights
questions.explain: A community admin is scoped to managing users within the partner's own Account hierarchy — it extends delegated administration without granting any internal Salesforce admin capability.

questions.q: Why do experienced architects treat Experience Cloud identity and sharing design as one combined workstream rather than two separate ones?
options: Because an identity-creation error (like a wrong Account link) immediately becomes a data-visibility problem, not just a login problem
Because sharing rules are configured entirely outside of Salesforce
Because identity and sharing are unrelated for external users
Because Experience Cloud has no sharing model at all
questions.explain: For external users, identity and authorization are tightly coupled — a mistake in how a user's Contact/Account gets linked at creation time directly causes incorrect data visibility, not merely a login issue.
